newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadians spend C$11.9 bln on home repair in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Canadians spend C$11.9 bln on home repair in 1996.

text.p: Canadians spent a total of C$11.9 billion on home repairs and renovations in 1996, about the same amount as in 1995, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.

On average, Canadian homeowners spent C$1,600 each on home repair and renovations in 1996, the lowest level since 1987, the first year the information was collected, StatsCan said. The average amount peaked at C$2,200 in 1989.
The average amount Canadians spent on contract work in 1996 was relatively stable at C$1,000, Statistics Canada said.
But homeowners spent about C$70 less each on work carried out by themselves in 1996, for an average of C$600, the federal agency said.
